source: Native Lambda SQS throttled batch ownership and recovery: two uniquely owned cleaned runs, four isolated single-message cases, real Node22 runtime and positive CloudWatch counters

documented_contract.function_code_failure: If your function code caused the error, Lambda stops processing and retrying the invocation. After queue visibility timeout runs out, the message reappears.
documented_contract.throttling: Lambda gradually backs off retries and continues to retry the message until its timestamp exceeds queue visibility timeout, at which point Lambda drops the message.
documented_contract.interpretation_boundary: Native corpus observes invocation/batch lease recovery, not deletion at throttled lease expiry; no exact internal scheduling contract inferred.

runs.source: Native AWS via boto3, real Node22 runtime; no caller receives, visibility changes, manual deletes, or CloudTrail trail during scenarios

findings.finding: Positive retained-lease retry: one sent and one polled/received source message, ESM InvokedEventCount=3 and FailedInvokeEventCount=2, function Throttles=2, then successful runtime record still ApproximateReceiveCount=1 and delete count1. Direct hold finished 10.008s after first receive; runtime began 0.962s later (10.970s after first receive), before 120s visibility expiry.
findings.scope: One batch containing one source message; actual failed internal Invoke request timestamps and pre-runtime receipt unavailable.

findings.finding: Capacity restored 33.030s after first receive, before 60s visibility deadline, but first successful runtime was at age60.024s with ApproximateReceiveCount=2. ESM polled2/invoked2/failed1/deleted1 and function Throttles=1.
findings.scope: Restoring capacity before expiry does not guarantee successful execution on the original lease in this bounded capture. This is not proof that AWS never retries retained batches.

findings.finding: 55-second direct hold occupied reserved concurrency1. Owned function reserved concurrency was set0 at 16:32:36.359184Z, then restored1 at 16:33:39.525233Z, after initial first-receive+60s deadline. First runtime at first-receive age120.048s had ApproximateReceiveCount=3. ESM polled3/invoked3/failed2/deleted1; function Throttles=2; SQS received3/deleted1.
findings.scope: Demonstrates fresh source receives across visibility boundaries and eventual recovery; does not expose exact timing/receipt of first two failed leases or prove a retained batch was retried on those leases.

findings.finding: Fresh control message ran at receive count1 and deliberately threw. Same source ID ran successfully at count2, 59.989s after first invocation and 60.030s after first receive, using a different receipt handle. ESM polled2/invoked2/failed1/deleted1, function Errors=1, Throttles=0; SQS received2/deleted1.
findings.scope: Contrasts ordinary function failure visibility redelivery with retained-lease throttled retry in the fast case.

findings.finding: Native ListMetrics positively published ESM counters with EventSourceMappingUUID alone. UUID-only queries returned positive counters. Initial supplemental FunctionName+UUID queries returned no datapoints despite positive UUID-only counters; empty results are retained as dimension mismatch evidence, not zero activity.
findings.scope: Observed dimensions in these runs, not exhaustive universal metric dimension enumeration.

production_implications: Retain a live received batch and its receipt context for throttled invocation retries without incrementing ReceiveCount or performing a new source receive; bound retry ownership by visibility.
Keep ordinary function-code failures on the SQS visibility/redelivery path rather than retrying the same live lease.
Lease expiry abandons only local batch ownership: it must not delete the source message; new receives advance ApproximateReceiveCount and issue new receipts.
Separate ESM attempt counts from source receive counts and billed function Invocations; the fast case has polled1, ESM invoked3, failed2, and one actual SQS runtime.
Do not encode observed timing as deterministic AWS backoff, capacity-restoration latency, or throughput. The 60s case did not recover before expiry despite restored capacity.
For native metric comparisons use positively discovered metric dimensions; FunctionName+UUID absence concealed real UUID-only ESM activity in the initial followup.
uncertainties: No ordinary trail was needed: runtime record identity, receive count and positive scoped service counters distinguish retained-lease retry in the fast case. Exact failed internal Invoke and source ReceiveMessage API inputs/outputs/receipt handles remain unobserved.
Approximate queue counters occasionally report zero while the single message is leased; those samples are retained and never treated as exact lease state.

Runtime ApproximateFirstReceiveTimestamp describes the first receive, not the exact time of subsequent receives. Later receipt timestamps are bounded by runtime plus visibility/receive-count evidence, not directly audited.
CloudWatch minute aggregates identify total attempts for isolated inputs, not per-attempt timing. Function Invocations includes warmup and accepted direct hold where used.
Capacity-zero in the late case is an explicit owned-function intervention; this run does not establish that it behaves identically to capacity held solely by an executing invocation.
No exact retry intervals, packing, scaling, throughput, or universal polling-deferral behavior is inferred.
